source.text: וּבִשְׁנַ֣ת אַחַ֗ת לְכ֨וֹרֶשׁ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ פָּרַ֔ס לִכְל֥וֹת דְּבַר־יְהוָ֖ה מִפִּ֣י יִרְמְיָ֑ה הֵעִ֣יר יְהוָ֗ה אֶת־ר֨וּחַ֙ כֹּ֣רֶשׁ מֶֽלֶךְ־פָּרַ֔ס וַיַּֽעֲבֶר־קוֹל֙ בְּכָל־מַלְכוּת֔וֹ וְגַם־בְּמִכְתָּ֖ב לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And in year one of Cyrus king of Persia, to fulfill [the] word of the LORD from [the] mouth of Jeremiah, stirred up the LORD the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he caused to pass a voice in all his kingdom, and also in writing, saying:

en.L: And in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, to fulfill the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the mouth of Jeremiah, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he caused a proclamation to pass through all his kingdom, and also in writing, saying:
en.B: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, so that the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoken by Jeremiah would be fulfilled, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he sent a proclamation throughout his whole kingdom and also put it in writing:
en.R: In the first year that Cyrus was king of Persia, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} moved Cyrus to act. This was so that the message {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had given through the prophet Jeremiah would come true. Cyrus sent an announcement through his whole kingdom and also put it in writing. It said:

es.L: Y en el primer año de Ciro rey de Persia, para que se cumpliera la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} de boca de Jeremías, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} despertó el espíritu de Ciro rey de Persia, el cual hizo pregonar por todo su reino, y también por escrito, diciendo:
es.B: En el primer año de Ciro rey de Persia, para que se cumpliera la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} anunciada por Jeremías, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} despertó el espíritu de Ciro rey de Persia, y él mandó pregonar por todo su reino, y también lo puso por escrito:
es.R: En el primer año del reinado de Ciro, rey de Persia, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} movió a Ciro a actuar. Así se cumplió el mensaje que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había dado por medio del profeta Jeremías. Ciro mandó anunciar un mensaje por todo su reino, y también lo hizo poner por escrito. Decía así:

sw.L: Na katika mwaka wa kwanza wa Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi, ili kulitimiza neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kutoka kinywa cha Yeremia, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaiamsha roho ya Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi, naye akapitisha tangazo katika ufalme wake wote, na pia kwa maandishi, akisema:
sw.B: Katika mwaka wa kwanza wa Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi, ili neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lililosemwa na Yeremia litimie, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliiamsha roho ya Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi, naye akaagiza tangazo litangazwe katika ufalme wake wote na kuandikwa pia:
sw.R: Katika mwaka wa kwanza wa utawala wa Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimgusa Koreshi moyoni ili atende. Hili lilitokea ili ujumbe ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa ameutoa kupitia nabii Yeremia utimie. Koreshi akatuma tangazo katika ufalme wake wote, akaagiza liandikwe pia. Lilisema:

decisions.choice: the first year of Cyrus king of Persia: his first year as ruler over Babylon and its lands
decisions.reason: Cyrus the Persian took Babylon in 539 BC, so his first year as its king began in 538 BC. Verses 1-3 repeat, almost word for word, the last verses of 2 Chronicles (36:22-23), so the story of the return picks up where Chronicles ends.

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD by Jeremiah: the promise that the exile would end after seventy years
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had said that Babylon would rule for seventy years and that then the LORD would bring his people back (Jeremiah 25:11-12; 29:10). 2 Chronicles 36:21-22 links the same promise to Cyrus. Isaiah also names Cyrus as the one who would say of Jerusalem, "Let it be rebuilt" (Isaiah 44:28; 45:1, 13).

decisions.choice: stirred up the spirit: moved him from within to act
decisions.reason: To stir up someone's spirit is to rouse their will so that they act (1 Chronicles 5:26; Haggai 1:14). The same words return in verse 5 for the people who went up: the LORD moves both the king and the exiles.

decisions.choice: caused a voice to pass: had a proclamation announced aloud
decisions.reason: The phrase means to have a message cried out through a territory (Exodus 36:6; 2 Chronicles 30:5). The decree was both proclaimed and written down.

decisions.choice: Readable adds "the prophet" and splits the sentence
decisions.reason: Readable says who Jeremiah was, which the reader may not know, and makes the purpose clause a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: "Ciro rey de Persia"; "despertó el espíritu" (L, B); "movió ... a actuar" (R)
decisions.reason: Ezra 1:1-3a is the same Hebrew as 2 Chronicles 36:22-23, so the published Spanish of Chronicles is reused word for word; only "de boca de" (Ezra: from the mouth) for Chronicles' "por boca de", and Readable's "el profeta" as the English Readable adds it, change.

decisions.choice: the Swahili wording of 2 Chronicles 36:22-23 reused at each level, changing only what the Hebrew changes ("kutoka kinywa cha Yeremia" for "from the mouth")
decisions.reason: Ezra 1:1-3a repeats the end of Chronicles almost word for word; keeping the published Swahili lets a reader see the parallel. Readable adds "nabii" and splits the sentence, as the English Readable does.

source.text: כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֗ר כֹּ֚רֶשׁ מֶ֣לֶךְ פָּרַ֔ס כֹּ֚ל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ נָ֣תַן לִ֔י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְהֽוּא־פָקַ֤ד עָלַי֙ לִבְנֽוֹת־ל֣וֹ בַ֔יִת בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּֽיהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: All [the] kingdoms of the earth has given to me the LORD, [the] God of the heavens, and he has appointed me to build for him a house in Jerusalem, which [is] in Judah.

en.L: Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: All the kingdoms of the earth {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of heaven, has given to me, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has appointed me to build {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a house in Jerusalem, which [is] in Judah.
en.B: This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has charged me to build {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.
en.R: This is the message of Cyrus king of Persia: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth. He has put me in charge of building a temple for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in Jerusalem, in Judah.

es.L: Así dice Ciro rey de Persia: Todos los reinos de la tierra me los ha dado {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de los cielos, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me ha encargado que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} edifique una casa en Jerusalén, que [está] en Judá.
es.B: Ciro rey de Persia dice esto: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de los cielos, me ha dado todos los reinos de la tierra, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me ha encargado que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} edifique una casa en Jerusalén, que está en Judá.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice Ciro, rey de Persia: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de los cielos, me ha dado todos los reinos de la tierra. Él me ha puesto a cargo de construir{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} un templo en Jerusalén, en Judá.

sw.L: Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi asema hivi: Falme zote za dunia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa mbinguni, amenipa, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} ameniagiza nimjengee nyumba huko Yerusalemu, ulioko Yuda.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo asemavyo Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa mbinguni, amenipa falme zote za dunia, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} ameniagiza nimjengee nyumba huko Yerusalemu, ulioko Yuda.
sw.R: Hili ndilo Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi analosema: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa mbinguni, amenipa falme zote za dunia. Amenipa kazi ya kumjengea hekalu huko Yerusalemu, katika Yuda.

decisions.choice: the God of heaven: a title for Israel's God used in the Persian period
decisions.reason: This title is common in Ezra, Nehemiah and Daniel (Ezra 5:11-12; 6:9-10; Nehemiah 1:4; Daniel 2:18). Persian kings honored the gods of the peoples they ruled; Cyrus's own inscription on a clay cylinder says he returned peoples and their gods' images to their homes and restored their shrines. In this decree he names the LORD as the giver of his empire.

decisions.choice: appointed me: gave me the task
decisions.reason: The verb used with "on me" means to put someone in charge of a task (Numbers 4:27; 2 Chronicles 36:23).

decisions.choice: a house: a temple
decisions.reason: A god's "house" is his temple (1 Kings 6:1; Ezra 1:3). The temple Solomon built had been destroyed by Babylon in 586 BC (2 Kings 25:9).

decisions.choice: a temple (Readable); a house (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "house", the word the book uses throughout; Readable says what the house is.

decisions.choice: "el Dios de los cielos"
decisions.reason: The title is the plural "the heavens" in Hebrew, and the Spanish of 2 Chronicles 36:23 has "el Dios de los cielos"; it is kept through Ezra (terms note).

decisions.choice: "un templo" (R); "una casa" (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in the English: Literal and Balanced keep "casa", the book's word; Readable says what the house is.

decisions.choice: "Mungu wa mbinguni" at every level; "nyumba" (L, B), "hekalu" (R)
decisions.reason: The title is the one of 2 Chronicles 36:23 and holds through the book; Readable says what the house is, as the English Readable does.

source.text: מִֽי־בָכֶ֣ם מִכָּל־עַמּ֗וֹ יְהִ֤י אֱלֹהָיו֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וְיַ֕עַל לִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּיהוּדָ֑ה וְיִ֗בֶן אֶת־בֵּ֤ית יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל ה֥וּא הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Who [is] among you from all his people, may be his God with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem which [is] in Judah, and let him build [the] house of the LORD, [the] God of Israel; he [is] the God who [is] in Jerusalem.

en.L: Whoever [is] among you of all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, may his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which [is] in Judah, and build the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] the God who [is] in Jerusalem.
en.B: Whoever among you belongs to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, may {{gender:their God be with them|his God be with him}}, and let {{gender:them|him}} go up to Jerusalem in Judah and build the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the God who is in Jerusalem.
en.R: Any of you who belong to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people may go up to Jerusalem in Judah and build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel. May your God be with you! He is the God whose temple is in Jerusalem.

es.L: Quien de entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} [sea] de todo {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo, su Dios [sea] con él, y suba a Jerusalén, que [está] en Judá, y edifique la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel; {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} [es] el Dios que [está] en Jerusalén.
es.B: Cualquiera de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que pertenezca a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo, que su Dios esté con él, y que suba a Jerusalén, en Judá, y edifique la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel; {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es el Dios que está en Jerusalén.
es.R: Todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} los que {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} subir a Jerusalén, en Judá, y construir el templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel. ¡Que {{plural_you:su Dios esté con ustedes|vuestro Dios esté con vosotros}}! Él es el Dios cuyo templo está en Jerusalén.

sw.L: Yeyote [aliye] kati yenu wa watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wote, Mungu wake na awe pamoja naye, naye apande Yerusalemu, ulioko Yuda, aijenge nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli; {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} [ndiye] Mungu aliye Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Yeyote kati yenu aliye wa watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, Mungu wake na awe pamoja naye, naye apande Yerusalemu katika Yuda, aijenge nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli; {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ndiye Mungu aliye Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Yeyote kati yenu aliye wa watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} anaweza kwenda Yerusalemu katika Yuda na kulijenga hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli. Mungu wenu na awe pamoja nanyi! Yeye ndiye Mungu ambaye hekalu lake liko Yerusalemu.

decisions.choice: his people: the LORD's people
decisions.reason: "His" refers back to the LORD, the God of heaven, in verse 2. The decree is addressed to all who belong to Israel's God, wherever they live in the empire.

decisions.choice: may his God be with him: a wish of blessing
decisions.reason: The words are a blessing on those who go, as in 2 Chronicles 36:23 ("the LORD his God be with him"). They also mean that the decree permits the journey; it does not order it.

decisions.choice: he is the God who is in Jerusalem: the God whose house stands in Jerusalem
alternatives: he is God, who is in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Cyrus, speaking as a ruler of many peoples, names the God of Israel by the place where he is worshiped. The clause could also be read with "he is God" as a confession on its own ("he is God, the one in Jerusalem"), but the shorter reading fits the way the decree speaks of the God of heaven.

decisions.choice: go up: travel to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Jerusalem stands in the hill country, and going there is always "going up" in Hebrew (Psalm 122:4). Here it also means coming back from exile (Ezra 2:1; 7:6).

decisions.choice: their God be with them / let them (Balanced), you (Readable)
decisions.reason: The decree speaks to each man, but whole families went up, women included (Ezra 2:65). Balanced uses the gender setting; Readable addresses the hearers as "you".

decisions.choice: "con él", "que suba", no gender setting; plural_you for "among you"
decisions.reason: As in 2 Chronicles 36:23: Spanish "él" after "quien" / "cualquiera" is the generic for anyone, man or woman, so the English gender setting has no Spanish counterpart. Readable speaks to the hearers, as the English Readable does, with the plural setting.

decisions.choice: no gender span: "Mungu wake na awe pamoja naye" and "apande" already cover men and women
alternatives: a gender span as in English
decisions.reason: Swahili pronouns and verb prefixes do not mark sex, so the English "them / him" choice has nothing to change in Swahili. This holds through Ezra.

source.text: וְכָל־הַנִּשְׁאָ֗ר מִֽכָּל־הַמְּקֹמוֹת֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר ה֣וּא גָֽר־שָׁם֒ יְנַשְּׂא֨וּהוּ֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י מְקֹמ֔וֹ בְּכֶ֥סֶף וּבְזָהָ֖ב וּבִרְכ֣וּשׁ וּבִבְהֵמָ֑ה עִם־הַ֨נְּדָבָ֔ה לְבֵ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And every [one] who remains, from all the places where he [is] sojourning there, let support him [the] men of his place with silver and with gold and with goods and with cattle, with the freewill offering for [the] house of God which [is] in Jerusalem.

en.L: And everyone who remains, in any of the places where he is sojourning, let the men of his place support him with silver and with gold and with goods and with livestock, besides the freewill offering for the house of God which [is] in Jerusalem.
en.B: And wherever any who are left are living as outsiders, let the people of that place help {{gender:them|him}} with silver and gold, with goods and livestock, as well as freewill offerings for the house of God in Jerusalem.
en.R: Those who are left are living in many places. The people where they live must help them. They should give them silver and gold, supplies and animals. They should also give gifts freely for God's temple in Jerusalem.

es.L: Y todo el que quede, de todos los lugares donde reside como forastero, que lo ayuden los hombres de su lugar con plata y con oro y con bienes y con ganado, además de la ofrenda voluntaria para la casa de Dios que [está] en Jerusalén.
es.B: Y dondequiera que vivan como forasteros los que hayan quedado, que la gente de ese lugar los ayude con plata y oro, con bienes y ganado, además de las ofrendas voluntarias para la casa de Dios en Jerusalén.
es.R: Los que han quedado viven en muchos lugares. La gente del lugar donde viven debe ayudarlos. Que les den plata y oro, provisiones y animales. Que también den ofrendas voluntarias para el templo de Dios en Jerusalén.

sw.L: Na kila aliyebaki, katika mahali popote anapokaa kama mgeni, watu wa mahali pake na wamsaidie kwa fedha na kwa dhahabu na kwa mali na kwa mifugo, zaidi ya sadaka ya hiari kwa ajili ya nyumba ya Mungu iliyoko Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Na popote wanapoishi kama wageni wale waliobaki, watu wa mahali hapo na wawasaidie kwa fedha na dhahabu, kwa mali na mifugo, pamoja na sadaka za hiari kwa ajili ya nyumba ya Mungu iliyoko Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Wale waliobaki wanaishi mahali pengi. Watu wa mahali wanapoishi lazima wawasaidie. Wawape fedha na dhahabu, mahitaji na wanyama. Pia watoe zawadi kwa hiari kwa ajili ya hekalu la Mungu huko Yerusalemu.

decisions.choice: everyone who remains: every survivor of God's people
decisions.reason: The word is used of the survivors who are left after the disaster of exile (Nehemiah 1:2-3; Isaiah 10:20-22). Each of them, wherever he lives, is to be helped to go up.

decisions.choice: the men of his place: his neighbors
alternatives: the Jews who stayed in that place
decisions.reason: The decree tells the neighbors to help the travelers. They may be the people of the land among whom the exiles lived, as the Egyptians gave silver and gold to Israel when it left Egypt (Exodus 12:35-36), or fellow Jews who stayed behind. The text does not say which; verse 6 says "all those around them" did so.

decisions.choice: the freewill offering: a gift given by choice, not required by law
decisions.reason: A freewill offering was given out of a willing heart, as for the tabernacle (Exodus 35:29; Leviticus 22:18). The help for the travelers is besides these gifts for the temple.

decisions.choice: is sojourning (Literal); living as outsiders (Balanced)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere, the verb for living where one has no rights of a native is "sojourn" at Literal and "live as an outsider" at Balanced.

decisions.choice: "reside como forastero" (L); "vivan como forasteros" (B)
decisions.reason: The verb for living where one is not a native: "forastero", as the published Spanish has it for the same verb (2 Chronicles 15:9).

decisions.choice: "anapokaa kama mgeni" (L), "wanapoishi kama wageni" (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is living where one is not a native; "mgeni" keeps that, as the English "sojourning" / "living as outsiders".

decisions.choice: "sadaka ya hiari" (L), "sadaka za hiari" (B), "zawadi kwa hiari" (R)
decisions.reason: The usual Swahili for a freewill offering, as in the Pentateuch drafts.

source.text: וַיָּק֜וּמוּ רָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָב֗וֹת לִֽיהוּדָה֙ וּבִנְיָמִ֔ן וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֑ם לְכֹ֨ל הֵעִ֤יר הָאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־רוּח֔וֹ לַעֲל֣וֹת לִבְנ֔וֹת אֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose [the] heads of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests and the Levites, of every [one whom] had stirred up God his spirit, to go up to build [the] house of the LORD which [is] in Jerusalem.

en.L: Then the heads of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin arose, and the priests and the Levites, everyone whose spirit God had stirred up, to go up to build the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} which [is] in Jerusalem.
en.B: Then the heads of the families of Judah and Benjamin got ready, with the priests and the Levites, everyone whose spirit God had stirred, to go up and build the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem.
en.R: Then the family leaders of Judah and Benjamin got ready to go, with the priests and the Levites. They were all people whose hearts God had moved to go up to Jerusalem and build the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} there.

es.L: Entonces se levantaron los jefes de las [casas] paternas de Judá y de Benjamín, y los sacerdotes y los levitas, todos aquellos cuyo espíritu Dios había despertado, para subir a edificar la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} que [está] en Jerusalén.
es.B: Entonces los jefes de las familias de Judá y de Benjamín se prepararon, junto con los sacerdotes y los levitas, todos aquellos cuyo espíritu Dios había despertado, para subir a edificar la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} en Jerusalén.
es.R: Entonces los jefes de familia de Judá y de Benjamín se prepararon para ir, junto con los sacerdotes y los levitas. Eran todos aquellos a quienes Dios les había movido el corazón para subir a Jerusalén y construir allí el templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Ndipo wakuu wa baba za Yuda na Benyamini wakainuka, na makuhani na Walawi, kila mmoja ambaye Mungu alikuwa ameiamsha roho yake, ili kupanda kuijenga nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} iliyoko Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Ndipo wakuu wa jamaa za Yuda na Benyamini walijiandaa, pamoja na makuhani na Walawi, kila mtu ambaye Mungu alikuwa ameiamsha roho yake, ili wapande kuijenga nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} iliyoko Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Ndipo viongozi wa jamaa za Yuda na Benyamini walijiandaa kwenda, pamoja na makuhani na Walawi. Wote hao walikuwa watu ambao Mungu alikuwa ameigusa mioyo yao ili waende Yerusalemu kulijenga hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} huko.

decisions.choice: the heads of the fathers: the heads of ancestral families
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here is short for "house of the fathers", the extended family traced through its male ancestor (Exodus 6:14). Its heads led the people in the return (Ezra 2:68; 8:1).

decisions.choice: Judah and Benjamin, the priests and the Levites
decisions.reason: Judah and Benjamin were the tribes of the southern kingdom that Babylon took into exile (2 Kings 24:14; 25:11; 1 Kings 12:21). The priests, descendants of Aaron, and the other Levites, who served at the temple, are named apart, as in the list in chapter 2 (2:36-42).

decisions.choice: whose spirit God had stirred: whom God moved to go
decisions.reason: The same words as in verse 1: God moved the king to let them go and moved the people to go.

decisions.choice: families (Balanced); family leaders, hearts (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "families" for "fathers", as the project does for the ancestral family. Readable says "hearts" for "spirit", the ordinary English for the seat of a person's will.

decisions.choice: "los jefes de las [casas] paternas" (L); "los jefes de las familias" (B); "los jefes de familia" (R)
decisions.reason: "Heads of the fathers" as the published Spanish of Chronicles renders it (1 Chronicles 15:12; 23:9); used through Ezra.

decisions.choice: "wakuu wa baba" (L), "wakuu wa jamaa" (B), "viongozi wa jamaa" (R); "roho" (L, B), "mioyo" (R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide for the heads of ancestral families in Ezra; "jamaa" is the word the Chronicles drafts use for the father's house, and Readable says "hearts" as the English does.

source.text: וְכָל־סְבִיבֹֽתֵיהֶם֙ חִזְּק֣וּ בִֽידֵיהֶ֔ם בִּכְלֵי־כֶ֧סֶף בַּזָּהָ֛ב בָּרְכ֥וּשׁ וּבַבְּהֵמָ֖ה וּבַמִּגְדָּנ֑וֹת לְבַ֖ד עַל־כָּל־הִתְנַדֵּֽב׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And all around them strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with goods, and with cattle, and with precious things, besides all freely offering.

en.L: And all those around them strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with goods, and with livestock, and with precious things, besides all that was freely offered.
en.B: Everyone around them supported them, giving silver vessels and gold, goods and livestock and costly gifts, besides everything that was given as a freewill offering.
en.R: All the people around them gave them help: things made of silver, gold, supplies, animals and expensive gifts. This was on top of all the gifts people freely gave for the temple.

es.L: Y todos los que estaban alrededor de ellos fortalecieron sus manos con objetos de plata, con oro, con bienes y con ganado, y con cosas preciosas, además de todo lo que se ofreció voluntariamente.
es.B: Todos sus vecinos los ayudaron, dándoles objetos de plata y oro, bienes, ganado y regalos valiosos, además de todo lo que se dio como ofrenda voluntaria.
es.R: Toda la gente de alrededor los ayudó: les dieron cosas de plata, oro, provisiones, animales y regalos caros. Esto fue además de todas las ofrendas que la gente dio de buena voluntad para el templo.

sw.L: Na wote waliowazunguka wakaitia nguvu mikono yao kwa vyombo vya fedha, kwa dhahabu, kwa mali, na kwa mifugo, na kwa vitu vya thamani, zaidi ya yote yaliyotolewa kwa hiari.
sw.B: Wote waliowazunguka waliwasaidia, wakawapa vyombo vya fedha na dhahabu, mali na mifugo na zawadi za thamani, zaidi ya yote yaliyotolewa kama sadaka za hiari.
sw.R: Watu wote waliowazunguka waliwasaidia: waliwapa vitu vya fedha, dhahabu, mahitaji, wanyama na zawadi za thamani kubwa. Hivi vilikuwa zaidi ya zawadi zote ambazo watu walitoa kwa hiari kwa ajili ya hekalu.

decisions.choice: strengthened their hands: helped and encouraged them
decisions.reason: To strengthen someone's hands is to support them so that they can do a task (Judges 9:24; Nehemiah 2:18; 6:9). Here the support is in goods.

decisions.choice: all around them: their neighbors
decisions.reason: The phrase picks up "the men of his place" from verse 4. It can include both other Jews and the people of the land; the text does not say.

decisions.choice: vessels of silver, with gold: silver objects and gold
decisions.reason: The list joins "vessels of silver" to bare "gold"; the gold may be gold objects or gold metal. The precious things are fine gifts of any kind (Genesis 24:53; 2 Chronicles 21:3).

decisions.choice: Readable adds "for the temple"
decisions.reason: The freewill offerings are the gifts for the house of God named in verse 4; Readable says so.

decisions.choice: "los ayudaron" (B, R); "fortalecieron sus manos" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the idiom, as Judges 9:24 does in Spanish; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m1).

decisions.choice: "waliwasaidia" (B, R); Literal keeps "wakaitia nguvu mikono yao"
decisions.reason: The idiom means practical help; here the help is in goods.

source.text: וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ כּ֔וֹרֶשׁ הוֹצִ֖יא אֶת־כְּלֵ֣י בֵית־יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוֹצִ֤יא נְבֽוּכַדְנֶצַּר֙ מִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖ם בְּבֵ֥ית אֱלֹהָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And the king Cyrus brought out the vessels of [the] house of the LORD which had brought out Nebuchadnezzar from Jerusalem and had put them in [the] house of his gods.

en.L: And King Cyrus brought out the vessels of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} which Nebuchadnezzar had brought out from Jerusalem and had put in the house of his gods.
en.B: King Cyrus also brought out the vessels of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken away from Jerusalem and placed in the house of his gods.
en.R: King Cyrus also brought out the bowls and other things that had belonged to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Nebuchadnezzar had taken them from Jerusalem and put them in the temple of his own gods.

es.L: Y el rey Ciro sacó los utensilios de la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} que Nabucodonosor había sacado de Jerusalén y había puesto en la casa de sus dioses.
es.B: El rey Ciro también sacó los utensilios de la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, que Nabucodonosor se había llevado de Jerusalén y había puesto en la casa de sus dioses.
es.R: El rey Ciro también sacó las vasijas y demás objetos que habían pertenecido al templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Nabucodonosor se los había llevado de Jerusalén y los había puesto en el templo de sus propios dioses.

sw.L: Na mfalme Koreshi akavitoa vyombo vya nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ambavyo Nebukadneza alikuwa amevitoa Yerusalemu na kuviweka katika nyumba ya miungu yake.
sw.B: Mfalme Koreshi pia alivitoa vyombo vya nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ambavyo Nebukadneza alikuwa amevichukua kutoka Yerusalemu na kuviweka katika nyumba ya miungu yake.
sw.R: Mfalme Koreshi pia alivitoa mabakuli na vitu vingine vilivyokuwa vya hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Nebukadneza alikuwa amevichukua kutoka Yerusalemu na kuviweka katika hekalu la miungu yake mwenyewe.

decisions.choice: the vessels Nebuchadnezzar took: the temple's gold and silver utensils
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took the temple's treasures in 597 BC and its bronze, gold and silver vessels when he burned it in 586 BC (2 Kings 24:13; 25:13-15; Daniel 1:2). Belshazzar drank from them at his feast (Daniel 5:2-3). Their return showed that the worship of the first temple went on in the second.

decisions.choice: his gods
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for God is plural in form and can mean "his god" or "his gods". Daniel 1:2 has the same phrase for the treasure house of Nebuchadnezzar's god. Either sense fits; the plural is kept.

decisions.choice: vessels (Literal, Balanced); bowls and other things (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word covers any object or utensil; here it is the basins, bowls and other items listed in verses 9-10. "Vessels" is kept so the word is the same through verse 11.

decisions.choice: "utensilios" (L, B); "vasijas y demás objetos" (R)
decisions.reason: The temple's vessels are "utensilios" in the published Spanish of 2 Chronicles 36:7, 18 at Literal and Balanced, "objetos" at Readable; the word is kept through verse 11.

decisions.choice: "vyombo" (L, B), "mabakuli na vitu vingine" (R)
decisions.reason: "Vyombo" covers any utensil and is kept through verse 11, as the English keeps "vessels".

source.text: וַיּֽוֹצִיאֵ֗םכּ֚וֹרֶשׁ מֶ֣לֶךְ פָּרַ֔ס עַל־יַ֖ד מִתְרְדָ֣ת הַגִּזְבָּ֑ר וַֽיִּסְפְּרֵם֙ לְשֵׁשְׁבַּצַּ֔ר הַנָּשִׂ֖יא לִיהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And brought them out Cyrus king of Persia by [the] hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and he counted them out to Sheshbazzar the leader of Judah.

en.L: And Cyrus king of Persia brought them out by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and he counted them out to Sheshbazzar the leader of Judah.
en.B: Cyrus king of Persia had them brought out by Mithredath the treasurer, who counted them out to Sheshbazzar the leader of Judah.
en.R: Cyrus king of Persia had Mithredath, the man in charge of his treasury, bring them out. Mithredath counted them and handed them over to Sheshbazzar, the leader of Judah.

es.L: Y Ciro rey de Persia los sacó por mano de Mitrídates el tesorero, y él los contó a Sesbasar, el jefe de Judá.
es.B: Ciro rey de Persia los hizo sacar por medio de Mitrídates el tesorero, quien se los contó a Sesbasar, el jefe de Judá.
es.R: Ciro, rey de Persia, hizo que Mitrídates, el encargado de su tesoro, los sacara. Mitrídates los contó y se los entregó a Sesbasar, el jefe de Judá.

sw.L: Na Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi akavitoa kwa mkono wa Mithredathi mtunza hazina, naye akamhesabia Sheshbaza kiongozi wa Yuda.
sw.B: Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi aliagiza vitolewe na Mithredathi mtunza hazina, naye akavihesabu na kumkabidhi Sheshbaza kiongozi wa Yuda.
sw.R: Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi alimwagiza Mithredathi, msimamizi wa hazina yake, avitoe. Mithredathi akavihesabu, akamkabidhi Sheshbaza, kiongozi wa Yuda.

decisions.choice: by the hand of: through, by means of
decisions.reason: The phrase names the official who did the work for the king (Exodus 9:35; 1 Kings 2:25).

decisions.choice: Mithredath the treasurer
decisions.reason: Mithredath is a Persian name, probably "given by Mithra". The word for treasurer is a Persian loanword (Ezra 7:21 has the Aramaic form).

decisions.choice: Sheshbazzar the leader of Judah
decisions.reason: Sheshbazzar has a Babylonian name. Cyrus made him governor and he laid the foundation of the temple (5:14-16). Whether he is the same man as Zerubbabel, who leads the return in 2:2 and 3:8, or as Shenazzar, a son of King Jehoiachin (1 Chronicles 3:18), is not settled; the text does not say.

decisions.choice: leader
decisions.reason: The word is "leader" at every level, as for the tribal leaders in Numbers; "prince" would suggest a king's son, which the text does not say.

decisions.choice: "Mitrídates", "Sesbasar", "el jefe de Judá"
decisions.reason: Mithredath in its usual Spanish form (the Persian name Mithradates) and Sesbasar as the terms note gives it; the title is "jefe" at every level, not "príncipe", which would suggest a king's son (as the English decision).

decisions.choice: "kiongozi" at every level
decisions.reason: As the English "leader": "mwana wa mfalme" would say he was a king's son, which the text does not say.

source.text: וְאֵ֖לֶּה מִסְפָּרָ֑ם אֲגַרְטְלֵ֨י זָהָ֜ב שְׁלֹשִׁ֗ים אֲגַרְטְלֵי־כֶ֨סֶף֙ אָ֔לֶף מַחֲלָפִ֖ים תִּשְׁעָ֥ה וְעֶשְׂרִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And these [were] their number: basins of gold thirty, basins of silver a thousand, knives nine and twenty,

en.L: And this [was] their number: thirty basins of gold, 1,000 basins of silver, twenty-nine knives,
en.B: This was their count: thirty gold basins, 1,000 silver basins, twenty-nine knives,
en.R: This is how many there were: thirty gold dishes, 1,000 silver dishes and twenty-nine knives.

es.L: Y este [era] su número: treinta tazones de oro, 1 000 tazones de plata, veintinueve cuchillos,
es.B: Esta fue su cuenta: treinta tazones de oro, 1 000 tazones de plata, veintinueve cuchillos,
es.R: Esta es la cantidad que había: treinta platos de oro, 1 000 platos de plata y veintinueve cuchillos.

sw.L: Na hii [ndiyo] idadi yake: sahani kubwa za dhahabu thelathini, sahani kubwa za fedha 1,000, visu ishirini na tisa,
sw.B: Hii ndiyo idadi yake: sahani kubwa thelathini za dhahabu, sahani kubwa 1,000 za fedha, visu ishirini na tisa,
sw.R: Idadi yake ilikuwa hii: sahani kubwa thelathini za dhahabu, sahani kubwa 1,000 za fedha na visu ishirini na tisa.

decisions.choice: basins: large dishes
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here in the Bible; it names a kind of basin or dish, probably for carrying offerings.

decisions.choice: knives
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It is related to a verb meaning to pass through or cut, so it is usually taken as knives for slaughtering sacrifices; it could also mean "replacements", that is, vessels of a second set.

decisions.choice: "tazones" (L, B); "platos" (R); "cuchillos"
decisions.reason: Rare words (m1, m2): a basin or dish, and knives, as the English reads them.

decisions.choice: "sahani kubwa" for the basins, kept apart from "mabakuli" (bowls) of verse 10
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here; a large dish keeps it distinct from the bowls listed next.

source.text: כְּפוֹרֵ֤י זָהָב֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֔ים כְּפ֤וֹרֵי כֶ֨סֶף֙ מִשְׁנִ֔ים אַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת וַעֲשָׂרָ֑ה כֵּלִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים אָֽלֶף׃ס

records.literal_gloss: bowls of gold thirty, bowls of silver of a second [kind] four hundred and ten, vessels other a thousand.

en.L: thirty bowls of gold, 410 bowls of silver of a second [kind], [and] 1,000 other vessels.
en.B: thirty gold bowls, 410 silver bowls of a second kind, and 1,000 other vessels.
en.R: There were also thirty gold bowls, 410 silver bowls of a lower quality and 1,000 other things.

es.L: treinta copas de oro, 410 copas de plata de segunda [clase], [y] 1 000 otros utensilios.
es.B: treinta copas de oro, 410 copas de plata de segunda clase y 1 000 utensilios más.
es.R: También había treinta copas de oro, 410 copas de plata de menor calidad y 1 000 objetos más.

sw.L: mabakuli ya dhahabu thelathini, mabakuli ya fedha ya [aina ya] pili 410, [na] vyombo vingine 1,000.
sw.B: mabakuli thelathini ya dhahabu, mabakuli 410 ya fedha ya aina ya pili, na vyombo vingine 1,000.
sw.R: Pia kulikuwa na mabakuli thelathini ya dhahabu, mabakuli 410 ya fedha ya hali ya chini, na vitu vingine 1,000.

decisions.choice: of a second kind: of lesser quality, or matching
decisions.reason: The word means "second" or "double". Here it probably marks bowls of a second grade, or a second set. The sense is not certain.

source.text: כָּל־כֵּלִים֙ לַזָּהָ֣ב וְלַכֶּ֔סֶף חֲמֵ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים וְאַרְבַּ֣ע מֵא֑וֹת הַכֹּ֞ל הֶעֱלָ֣ה שֵׁשְׁבַּצַּ֗ר עִ֚ם הֵעָל֣וֹת הַגּוֹלָ֔ה מִבָּבֶ֖ל לִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: All [the] vessels of gold and of silver [were] five thousand and four hundred; the whole brought up Sheshbazzar with [the] bringing up of the exile from Babylon to Jerusalem.

en.L: All the vessels of gold and of silver [were] 5,400. All [this] Sheshbazzar brought up when the exiles were brought up from Babylon to Jerusalem.
en.B: In all there were 5,400 vessels of gold and silver. Sheshbazzar brought all of them up when the exiles were brought up from Babylon to Jerusalem.
en.R: Altogether there were 5,400 gold and silver objects. Sheshbazzar brought all of them with him when the people who had been in exile came back from Babylon to Jerusalem.

es.L: Todos los utensilios de oro y de plata [eran] 5 400. Todo [esto] lo subió Sesbasar cuando subieron los desterrados de Babilonia a Jerusalén.
es.B: En total eran 5 400 utensilios de oro y de plata. Sesbasar los llevó todos cuando los desterrados subieron de Babilonia a Jerusalén.
es.R: En total había 5 400 objetos de oro y de plata. Sesbasar los llevó todos consigo cuando los que habían estado en el destierro regresaron de Babilonia a Jerusalén.

sw.L: Vyombo vyote vya dhahabu na vya fedha [vilikuwa] 5,400. Vyote [hivyo] Sheshbaza akavipandisha wakati watu wa uhamisho walipopandishwa kutoka Babeli hadi Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Vyombo vyote vya dhahabu na vya fedha vilikuwa 5,400. Sheshbaza alivipandisha vyote wakati watu wa uhamisho walipopandishwa kutoka Babeli kwenda Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Jumla ya vitu vya dhahabu na fedha ilikuwa 5,400. Sheshbaza alivileta vyote pamoja naye wakati watu waliokuwa uhamishoni waliporudi kutoka Babeli kwenda Yerusalemu.

decisions.choice: 5,400: a total larger than the items listed
decisions.reason: The items in verses 9-10 add up to 2,499, not 5,400. Either the list names only the main items, or numbers have been changed in copying, which happens easily with numbers. The Greek book of 1 Esdras (2:13-14) gives different figures for the items and a total of 5,469. The Hebrew numbers are kept as they stand.

decisions.choice: the exile: the community of exiles
decisions.reason: The word means both the exile and the people in exile (Ezra 2:1; 4:1). It is the book's name for those who came back.

decisions.choice: the people who had been in exile
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the exile" as the people, following the book-wide choice.

decisions.choice: "los desterrados" (L, B); "los que habían estado en el destierro" (R)
decisions.reason: The exile as the community of exiles (m2); "destierro" as in Kings and Chronicles, and Readable says it is the people, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "watu wa uhamisho" (L, B), "watu waliokuwa uhamishoni" (R)
decisions.reason: "Uhamisho" is both the exile and the exiles; the book-wide terms are "wana wa uhamisho" (L) and "waliorudi kutoka uhamishoni" (B, R).
